evidence.title: HumanLayer
evidence.locator: Platform; Pricing
evidence.finding: Current brand HumanLayer; task-centered workspace and free Starter for up to three members and 200 monthly sessions. Pro $100/user/month.

evidence.title: How HumanLayer tasks work
evidence.locator: Task versus session; Share and review; Task files
evidence.finding: One task groups sessions, synced artifacts and review; human permissions control edits/comments; files sync across workstations.

evidence.title: How Remote Daemons Work
evidence.locator: Hosts; Process lifecycle; Browser capabilities
evidence.finding: User host runs Claude/Codex; web/phone UI can message sessions. Persistent supervision required; browser lacks terminal/workspace configuration.

evidence.title: HumanLayer Docs
evidence.locator: Guides and explanations
evidence.finding: Official guides cover remote daemons, workflows, Codex, Bedrock, external issue sources and automation.

evidence.title: HumanLayer is joining Factory
evidence.locator: November 4 announcement; transition period and export/migration/self-hosting paragraph
evidence.finding: HumanLayer announced it is joining Factory on November 4, 2026. The current platform stays available during a transition of at least 30 days, with data export, Factory migration or open-source self-hosting support and refunds for recent paying customers. No exact hosted shutdown date is stated.

evidence.title: Running a HumanLayer task
evidence.locator: Before you start; installation; task and session creation
evidence.finding: The tutorial uses the Apple-silicon macOS app, signed-in Claude Code, Git and an inline task. Oneshot can run directly in a checkout; other host operating systems use remote-daemon instructions. No setup timing was measured.

evidence.title: How Remote Daemons Work
evidence.locator: Hosts; authentication; disposable hosts; process lifecycle; browser limitations; security
evidence.finding: Desktop and remote daemons run Claude/Codex on user-selected hosts. The phone/browser can start, watch and message sessions but lacks workspace configuration and embedded terminals. Long-running supervision and persisted host credentials/history are required; running sessions fail after roughly two minutes without a responding host.

evidence.title: Run a remote daemon
evidence.locator: Install; login or launch token; systemd; daemon updates
evidence.finding: The CLI installs on the user host. Interactive device login persists credentials; launch tokens authenticate one process. A documented systemd user service or another supervisor keeps the daemon alive. npm daemons can update from the app; Windows updates manually.

evidence.title: How HumanLayer tasks keep related work together
evidence.locator: Task/session distinction; share and review; task files
evidence.finding: Tasks group separately configured sessions and shared files. Editors add sessions and edit files; reviewers comment. Supported agent file tools sync text, HTML, images and PDFs into the artifact view, including across workstations. This is not a repository backup.

evidence.title: Workspace setup
evidence.locator: Before you start; Configure with agent; checks; troubleshooting
evidence.finding: Workspace setup uses local Git repositories, branches and one or several task worktrees. A configuration skill proposes shared/local JSON, source refs, setup commands and files to copy. Failed setup can require manual diagnosis.

evidence.title: How workspace configuration works
evidence.locator: Primary repository; effective configuration; task workspace
evidence.finding: Shared and local JSON configure separate worktrees for each repository; setup commands and copied files apply per repository. Skills/instructions load across repositories, while MCP and Claude settings follow the launch directory.

evidence.title: Run a workflow in HumanLayer
evidence.locator: Select workflow; phases; changing plans; finish
evidence.finding: Oneshot, RPI, PRD-Oriented and Freeform are distinct paths. Users review and amend saved artifacts; later artifacts take precedence. PR creation is a separate skill/action. Freeform has no fixed phases.

evidence.title: Skills and workflows reference
evidence.locator: Workflow choices; artifact precedence; checkpoints; implementation; PR output; auto-advance
evidence.finding: RPI skills create and revise task artifacts, split implementation into checked phases and use manual or selected automatic handoffs. PR skills compare the branch diff with the plan, create/update a PR and save a description or optional walkthrough. These are documented agent workflows, not verified delivery enforcement.

evidence.title: Sub-agent models and effort
evidence.locator: Claude Code and Codex tables; Faster Research Subagents; exclusions
evidence.finding: RPI uses named research/implementation subagents with harness-specific model/effort rules. Claude uses fixed model aliases or inherit; Codex children use the parent model with role-specific effort. Experiments control faster research; project/user definitions can differ.

evidence.title: Set Up Codex CLI
evidence.locator: Authentication; custom Responses endpoint; select model/effort
evidence.finding: The HumanLayer CLI supports Codex browser/device authentication, configurable OpenAI Responses, Bedrock and Azure endpoints, model selection and reasoning effort. Endpoint credentials and model compatibility have explicit restrictions.

evidence.title: Route models through an LLM gateway
evidence.locator: Gateway and provider configuration
evidence.finding: Documents user-configured model gateways/proxies; endpoint settings and daemon environment determine the provider route. This is distinct from a universal harness adapter or a verified local-model setup.

evidence.title: Connect GitHub and Create Tasks from Issues
evidence.locator: Install permissions; create task; source-issue artifact links
evidence.finding: Organization admins connect repository-scoped GitHub Apps. Issue details/comments enter ticket.md, and artifact links update one source-issue comment. Failed link updates do not block saving an artifact.

evidence.title: Connect Linear and Run Ticket Workflows
evidence.locator: Create task; RPI workflow states; CLI
evidence.finding: Linear OAuth imports issues and synchronizes named workflow states and artifact links. The separate Linear CLI can inspect/manage states and update issues; this is external issue management.

evidence.title: Connect Jira and Create Tasks from Tickets
evidence.locator: Before you start; create and check task
evidence.finding: Organization admins authorize Jira Cloud. Tasks can start from accessible tickets; reconnect/disconnect and import toggles are documented. It does not establish complete two-way field synchronization.

evidence.title: Run HumanLayer Sessions in Automations
evidence.locator: How it works; tasks/sessions; personal access token; GitHub Actions
evidence.finding: automation run creates/reuses a task and runs one Cloud-visible session in a user-supplied CI/cron checkout. It uses a PAT and provider credentials, starts a job-local daemon with permission prompts bypassed, streams events and exits with session result. Scheduling, concurrency and no-op guards belong to the external workflow.

evidence.title: HumanLayer release notes
evidence.finding: Recent releases add directory-task worktrees, multiplayer beta UI, orchestration/teleport skills, Pi streaming, diff comments and attention notifications. Earlier entries document live shared drafts, harness handoff, public review links, usage-limit recovery, host load and opt-in GitHub PR controls.

evidence.title: HumanLayer platform and pricing
evidence.locator: Starter; Pro; Enterprise; FAQ; Security
evidence.finding: Starter advertises up to three members and 200 sessions/month. Pro is USD 100/user/month with BYO subscriptions/API keys; Enterprise lists SSO/SAML and a SOC 2 Type II assertion. The undated open-source FAQ is stale relative to the October 23 announcement; pricing is read in the November 4 transition context.

evidence.title: Open sourcing HumanLayer
evidence.locator: October 23; what is inside; running it yourself
evidence.finding: The vendor identifies the current desktop/web application, daemon/CLI, API and sync proxy as Apache-2.0 core matching Cloud. Self-hosting setup still requires third-party keys; future deployment guides remain plans. Self-build telemetry is disabled unless configured.

evidence.title: HumanLayer README.md
evidence.locator: What is here; get started; self-hosting; license
evidence.finding: The pinned current application repository includes desktop/web, daemon, CLI and server components and supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. It identifies Electron/Tauri macOS shells, a local devstack and telemetry controls through unset environment configuration.

evidence.title: HumanLayer LICENSE
evidence.locator: Apache License version 2.0
evidence.finding: The current application repository carries Apache-2.0; the README names separately licensed vendored MIT folders.

evidence.title: HumanLayer apps/riptide-humanlayer-claude-plugin/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md
evidence.locator: Job table and rules
evidence.finding: The built-in orchestration skill uses the HumanLayer CLI to choose hosts, launch tasks and sessions, inspect statuses/PRs and manage task artifacts. This is a product-supplied skill, not evidence of an independently tested cross-harness team.

evidence.title: HumanLayer apps/riptide-humanlayer-claude-plugin/skills/orchestrate/references/list-tasks.md
evidence.locator: Task list and session status table
evidence.finding: The CLI lists persistent task IDs/slugs, owner filters and archive metadata. This reference explicitly says a task has no status of its own; draft/running/needs-approval/usage-limit/failed states belong to sessions.

evidence.title: HumanLayer apps/riptide-humanlayer-claude-plugin/skills/orchestrate/references/launch-task.md
evidence.locator: Project and workspace-spec launch; setup checks
evidence.finding: CLI examples create the same task/workspace UUID and launch sessions, including tasks without external tickets. Repository materialization/errors are inspectable; copy/setup command errors need not block launch. Existing-folder execution is allowed explicitly.

evidence.title: HumanLayer apps/riptide-humanlayer-claude-plugin/skills/orchestrate/references/launch-session.md
evidence.locator: Launch in project; choices for both
evidence.finding: CLI examples launch sessions under a task ID, configure host/agent/model and choose default, accept_edits, auto or bypass permissions. Another host uses the pushed task branch; unpushed work stays behind.

evidence.title: HumanLayer apps/cli/src/api/proxy-router.ts
evidence.locator: EXCLUDED_ROUTE_GROUPS; applySyncDefaults; createProxyRouter
evidence.finding: The CLI proxies the product RPC contract except metrics and requires scoped filters for conversation-event sync. This supports product-owned API access, not a stability guarantee or an exposed MCP server.

evidence.title: HumanLayer Claude provider login driver
evidence.locator: apps/riptide-daemon/src/effects/services/provider-login/drivers/claude-login-driver.ts lines 34-88 (AUTH_LOGIN_ARGS, runLogin), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: The daemon's Claude sign-in spawns the installed Claude Code CLI with `auth login` / `auth status`, so the CLI's own account login (including subscription sign-in) is used; the Codex driver separately runs ChatGPT device sign-in.

evidence.title: HumanLayer Claude session launch
evidence.locator: apps/riptide-daemon/src/effects/services/claude-sessions/prepare-claude-session.ts lines 172-176 (locateClaudeExecutable; pathToClaudeCodeExecutable at line 384), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: Claude sessions locate the user's installed claude executable (configured path or PATH) and pass it to the Agent SDK as pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, so sessions run on the local Claude Code install and its login.

evidence.title: HumanLayer release notes 0.149.0
evidence.locator: apps/docs/release-notes.md lines 675-692 (0.149.0, July 27, 2026, Other Changes), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: Release 0.149.0 notes that task and session lists were stabilised so rows stop reshuffling while agents run in parallel, i.e. several sessions run at once in the shipped app.

evidence.title: HumanLayer built-in skill: list tasks
evidence.locator: apps/riptide-humanlayer-claude-plugin/skills/orchestrate/references/list-tasks.md lines 1-10 (list-tasks reference), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: The bundled orchestration reference states that a task has no status of its own; only its sessions carry statuses. Tasks can be listed, paged, filtered by owner and archived.

evidence.title: HumanLayer remote daemons explanation
evidence.locator: apps/docs/explanation/remote-daemons.md lines 66-113 (Daemon hosts; Containers; Disposable and suspended hosts), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: A daemon host can be a cloud VM, workstation or private-network machine, and the docs explain running the daemon inside a container (credential volume) and on disposable/suspended VMs. The daemon is the host; the docs do not describe HumanLayer creating a container or VM per session.

evidence.title: HumanLayer desktop versioning
evidence.locator: apps/riptide-native/README.md lines 11-13 (Versioning), commit f9bd735
evidence.finding: Desktop releases derive their version at build time and every merge to main ships a new auto-updated version, so the pinned main commit corresponds to shipped builds (GitHub Releases only hold old codelayer pre-releases).

evidence.title: HumanLayer homepage pricing and FAQ (checked 2026-11-10)
evidence.locator: Pricing section and FAQ, fetched 2026-11-10
evidence.finding: Starter is free for teams of up to three members and 200 sessions/month; Pro is USD 100 per user per month; Enterprise is custom-priced and adds SSO/SAML, audit logs and on-prem/private VPC. FAQ: bring existing Claude/Codex subscriptions or API keys, no separate HumanLayer per-token bill. A free macOS (Apple silicon) download and Homebrew cask are offered.

evidence.title: HumanLayer coding-agent schema
evidence.locator: CODING_AGENT_VALUES; LAUNCHABLE_CODING_AGENT_VALUES; isLaunchableCodingAgent
evidence.finding: The closed coding-agent schema contains Claude aliases, CodeLayer/Fold, Pi, OpenCode and Codex. Only the declared launchable subset is offered by task launchers; absent values are rejected by daemon handlers. Other supported terminal agents can be mirrored. No Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok, Aider or Antigravity type is present.
